newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed, within downtrends.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed, within downtrends.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mixed Monday, on low volumes, as the complex continued to consolidate following the downtrend of the past month, analysts said.
"The best you can say about it that we're back up near resistance at the top of the downtrend channel, especially in gold," North American Equity Services floor trader John Geraghty said.
COMEX December gold ended unchanged at $382.60 an ounce, after trading in a $383.80-381.80 range.
In bullion trade, spot gold ended quoted $380.35/380.85 an ounce, compared to the London Monday afternoon fix at $380.10, and Friday's New York close around $380.25.
COMEX gold stocks fell 141,120 ounces to 1,120,513 ounces Friday, and are down 273,280 ounces in the last eight days, equivalent to about 2,700 COMEX contracts, analysts noted.

The December 1996/December 1997 gold spread ended at $14.30 an ounce, after dipping to $13.50 last week. Producers may be tempted to hedge on further bounces to lock in the contango, as the 12 month spread is threatening to break down out of its nine month $14.00-$17.00 range, traders said.
"We expect to see good forward selling from producers at $385.00 basis spot and above," Merrill Lynch analyst Ted Arnold said in a weekly report.
"We suspect that $370 will be broken in time because physical demand in large parts of Asia is very poor," he said.
"There is also likely to be much more European central bank selling next year in order to help meet the Maastricht criteria for monetary union," he said.
COMEX December silver ended up 1.3 cents at $4.888 an ounce, after trading in a $4.860-4.910 range.
NYMEX January platinum ended up 60 cents at $388.60 an ounce, while NYMEX December palladium closed down $1.85 cents at $119.75.
